predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: the Byzantine cities of Nicaea and briefly Nicomedia, gained 1075-1081

predecessors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
predecessors.text: the plateau around Iconium and Ankara that Rum held after 1097; the page does not locate the Seljuk-held land at the secession

successors.name: Beylik of Karaman (Karamanids)
successors.text: Konya and the plateau; the infobox gives 'Karamanid conquest: 1308', and the Karamanids conquered a relative's lands, a brief holder of Konya, in 1328

successors.name: Ilkhanate
successors.text: Anatolia under Ilkhanid administration: 'Seljuk power declined until the dynasty died out in 1308, and its territories passed to the Ilkhanate' (Köse Dağ page)

ledger.x: 1077: Suleiman ibn Qutalmish founds the Sultanate of Rum at Nicaea.
1097: the Byzantines retake the western cities.
1097: the capital moves from Nicaea to Iconium (Konya) (infobox 'Iconium (Konya), 1097-1308'); the Byzantine-Seljuk wars page has Iconium the capital 'around 1101'.
19 June 1097: Nicaea surrenders to the Byzantines.
1174: Sivas absorbed.
1178: Malatya occupied.
Page silent: no page opened dates these gains.
1190: Holy Roman Empire forces reach Konya during the Third Crusade.
1190: the crusaders leave Konya; the page calls the occupation temporary.
1202: Erzurum is taken from the Saltukids.
1207: Kaykhusraw I takes Antalya.
1211: the court moves to Sivas (infobox 'Sebastia (Sivas), 1211-1220'); the Kaykaus I page does not call Sivas a capital.
1211-1212: Tughril of Erzurum secedes.
1214: Trebizond becomes a Rum vassal.
1214: Kaykaus I takes Sinop.
1221: Konya is again the only capital.
1221: Kayqubad I takes Alanya.
1225: Cilician Armenia becomes a Rum vassal.
1230: Erzurum annexed.
ledger.cp: Jahan Shah of Erzurum (Seljuk cadet branch)

ledger.x: 1230: Kayqubad finally defeats Jalal al-Din at Yassıçimen 'between Sivas and Erzincan in 1230' and establishes Seljuq rule over 'Erzurum, Ahlat, and the Lake Van region, which had been Ayyubid territory'.
1234: Kayqubad defeats the Ayyubids.
1237: Kaykhusraw II takes the Diyarbakır region.
1242: the Mongols take Erzurum.
1243: Baiju invades Rum again.
26 June 1243: the Mongols crush Kaykhusraw II at Köse Dağ and then capture Kayseri, Sivas, Erzincan and Ankara; Rum 'was reduced to the status of a client kingdom' and the sultans swore allegiance.
1243: Trebizond leaves Rum's overlordship.
1244: Cilicia submits to the Mongols and leaves Rum's overlordship.
1250: the east passes under Mongol administration.
October 1256: Bayju defeats Kaykaus II near Aksaray.
October 1256: Rum becomes an Ilkhanid vassal; Kaykaus II kept the west until he fled to Crimea in 1260.

Page silent on the extent: in 1260 Kaykaus II fled to Crimea and the west ceased to have a sultan of its own; Cliopatria has no Rum shape for 1260-1304 and covers the land with the Mongol Empire (and then the Ilkhanate).
1277: the Karamanids take Konya.
1277: the Karamanid hold on Konya is brief ('briefly installing Jimri as a puppet ruler'); the page does not say who retook it or when.
1303: the court is at Kayseri.
1308: the last sultan is murdered and the Seljuks of Rum end.

wars.name: First Crusade (Anatolian campaign)
wars.outcome: Kilij Arslan I defeated the People's Crusade in 1096 but was beaten by the princely armies and driven back into south-central Anatolia; Nicaea surrendered to the Byzantines on 19 June 1097 and John Doukas retook the western cities.

wars.name: Byzantine campaigns against Konya
wars.outcome: Manuel I campaigned against Konya in 1146 (no result given) and was attacked near Kotyaeion on his return from Antioch in 1159 after Kilij Arslan II refused passage; no border moved.

wars.name: Danishmend conquest by Kilij Arslan II
wars.outcome: Kilij Arslan II attacked Yaghibasan in 1155, absorbed the Sivas lands when Nur ad-Din died in 1174 and occupied Malatya in 1178, ending Danishmend rule.

wars.name: Battle of Myriokephalon
wars.outcome: Seljuk victory on 17 September 1176; Manuel I demolished the fort at Sublaeum but left Dorylaeum, and Turks raided the Meander valley in 1177.

wars.name: Third Crusade at Konya
wars.outcome: Forces of the Holy Roman Empire made 'a temporary occupation of Konya in 1190'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Rum-Georgia war and Battle of Basiani
wars.outcome: Suleiman II was defeated by Georgia under Tamar and withdrew to Erzurum; the page gives 1203 or 1204 and no land change.

wars.name: Rum-Nicaea war and Battle of Antioch on the Meander
wars.outcome: Kaykhusraw I seized Antalya from its Nicaean garrison in 1207 and was killed at Antioch on the Meander in 1211; Kaykaus I then made a treaty with Theodore Laskaris.

wars.name: Siege of Sinope
wars.outcome: Alexios of Trebizond, captured by Turkmen, handed Sinop over and accepted vassalage; the walls were rebuilt April-September 1215.

wars.name: Kayqubad I's coastal and Cilician campaigns
wars.outcome: Alanya taken in 1221; Trebizond besieged in 1222-1223 and forced to renew vassalage; Cilician Armenia reduced to a vassal state in 1225.

wars.name: Battle of Yassıçemen and the Khwarazmian war
wars.outcome: Jalal al-Din took Ahlat; Kayqubad defeated him at Yassıçimen in 1230 and annexed Erzurum, Ahlat and the Lake Van region.

wars.name: Rum-Ayyubid war of 1234
wars.outcome: Kayqubad 'completely defeated the allied Ayyubid forces' in 1234 and took Siverek, Urfa, Harran and Raqqa.

wars.name: Battle of Köse Dağ
wars.outcome: The Mongols under Baiju took Erzurum in 1242 and crushed Kaykhusraw II on 26 June 1243; Rum became a client kingdom paying tribute.

wars.name: Battle of Aksaray
wars.outcome: Bayju defeated Kaykaus II on 14 October 1256 and 'all of Anatolia became officially subject to Möngke Khan'.

wars.name: Battle of Elbistan and the Karamanid capture of Konya
wars.outcome: After Baibars beat the Mongols at Elbistan the Karamanids captured Konya and installed a puppet, Jimri, briefly.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines are given by any page; the frontiers with the Byzantines, the beyliks and the Armenian and Ayyubid lands are approximate throughout, and from 1243 the sultanate's extent is blurred by Mongol administration.
